summary: Fixed two related node-adoption control-channel gaps that could leave a mymatasan/myiotsan node effectively unmanageable from the myseliasan control plane. First, if a node's adopt call succeeded but the control plane then failed to save the resulting ManagedNode row (a DB hiccup or schema mismatch), the node had already committed to pairing and burned its single-use claim code - it was left permanently stranded, invisible to discovery and unable to retry. NodeRegistry.Adopt now best-effort rolls back the node's own pairing in that case (so it becomes discoverable and adoptable again) and returns a new ErrAdoptPersist with an actionable operator-facing message instead of a raw database error, while the raw cause is still logged server-side. Second, a node that already holds a valid fleet-CA certificate but has no managed record (e.g. released here without being reset on the node) kept dialing the control channel and being silently refused forever, with no operator-visible symptom beyond a repeating log line. ControlServer now tracks each refusal (deduped by node id, bounded at 200 entries) and a new Unrecognized nodes panel in the Nodes UI lists them (GET /api/nodes/unrecognized) with Block (POST /api/nodes/{id}/block, revokes the certificate via a new RevokeNode registry method that needs no managed row) and Dismiss (POST /api/nodes/{id}/forget) actions. AcceptControlConn was also reordered to check certificate revocation before the row lookup, so a blocked-but-row-less node correctly reports as revoked rather than a generic unknown node that would make Block appear to do nothing.
compatibility: Backward compatible; purely additive visibility + a failure-path fix. No behavior change for a node that adopts and connects normally. The Unrecognized nodes panel renders nothing when there are no stranded connections, which is the default/existing-install state. No schema change and no migration - RejectedNode tracking is in-memory on the running ControlServer only. This is a myseliasan-scoped fix and does not touch mymatasan, myidsan, or myiotsan.
